name: The Elder Scrolls III: Morrowind Game of the Year Edition

data: Morrowind's combination of amazing music, immersive story, and fantastic RPG elements definitely make it one of the best games I've ever played
Great story with amazing gameplay and world
it is still an amazing game, and worth playing, especially with mods
Ladies and Gentleman I absolutely recommend Morrowind for everyone who likes great story, beautiful world and diverse quests in their RPG games
Easily the best Elder Scrolls game by far, compelling conflicts a good variety of factions and unique items, interesting quests and, imo, the best mods
Gameplay is not difficult, it's just tiresome and frustrating
the problems make it unplayable for me

Best Elder Scrolls Game.
Skills actually need to be a main or side skill to be anywhere near useful.
Graphics are like what you would expect from a game from 2002.
Leveling up is actually satisfying late game, enemies are tough at first and gradually get easier and easier.
Nothing is handed to you, you have to figure it out.
The third Elder Scrolls game does not disappoint in the least. The best of them, in my opinion, and the best stories of all.

I spent a wonderfully irresponsible amount of time playing it on Xbox as a kid. We're talking thousands of hours. Sure, half of that was spent staring at a loading screen, but still. Good times.

Not just the best Elder Scrolls, but possibly the best RPG I have ever played (minus the Zelda games). In its day, Morrowind was mindblowingly dense and gave the true feeling of living in another world. I spent 600 hours + with this game before I had a STEAM account, and didn't even come close to exploring all of it. My personal quest was to score a Glass War Axe, as shown in the loading screens... it took me a few years to find one. The mechanics are tough to figure out at first, but eventually you get a feel for the gameplay and combat system (missed sword swings are based on a dice-roll system, you will eventually level past missing enemies). Can't wait for Skywind!

One of my favorite games of all times, but it has various aspects that may be hard to like in 2024 without nostalgia goggles.

Cities/towns are copy paste of similar buildings that are kind of boring, combat mechanics will feel weird to newcomers and a lot of quests are not really interesting. I like the UI as opposed to the console oriented modern UIs but a lot of people disagree with me on this.

The world and the main story are alright and like most Bethesda games there's a lot of lore and stuff to discover and enjoy. The land of Morrowind is breathtaking, it does not feel like the "standard European fantasy setting" which still stands out from other entries in the Elder Scroll series.

When I was younger I loved keeping a notebook and pen with me, taking notes, writing down directions to the cave I have to find to retrieve the random artifact, names of people and how they relate to each other, how I can take advantage of all this information. I don't know If I can dedicate myself at this level to a game released in 2024. These things no longer charm me, but when it comes to Morrowind I still enjoy it.

I'd still recommend people to try it out with Open MW or something similar and decide for themselves.

Morrowind is a strange beast of a game. The soundtrack is tiny, the graphics primitive for its 2002 release date, its underlying mechanics convoluted and archaic. But if you're patient and willing to deal with its datedness, it offers tons of content, compelling stories, and options for resolving quests.

Mods are a necessity for Morrowind unless you're a masochist. I also recommend having the UESP (Unofficial Elder Scrolls Pages) as a reference guide to tab to/read on a second monitor. (They have thorough info about locations, items, quests, NPCs, and so on and will save you a lot of frustration.)

Do not bother buying this game if you're uncomfortable with heavy modding and/or archaic Western RPG mechanics. It's so clunky that you probably won't enjoy it.
A classic in the genre, and with the newest graphic mods, it is a beautiful game even by today's standards. Well worth buying.
While the exploration and enviroments are fine, the combat and graphics are heavily dated and rather boring now. Oh, and the music's good. All three tracks of it.

genuinely so much more rewarding than the future games. It takes some time to get used to, since your character actually has very limited capabilities early, that are entirely dependent on race and class.

Usually by level like 5 you'll have the game figured out and by 10 you'll be a walking god.

If you finish a faction quest line, you actually feel like a legendary powerful figure who has earned respect.
I will never forget the Telvanni quest line, by the end you are so magically powerful it's unreal you actually feel that you deserve to be the head of the faction. Unlike any of the future games, where you can be head of the mages guild before level 3.

Can't wait to make a new character, and do the appropriate factions.

When I initially booted this game up, I was taken aback by the sheer openness of the world it provided. As someone who has grown up with mission markers and waypoints dotting the UI, I was at first frustrated by having to find my own way based solely upon somewhat vague directions provided by a wary quest giver. However, after spending a bit more time with the game and acclimating myself to the seemingly archaic design decisions, I managed to find myself immersed in a world like no other with top-shelf map design making it a cinch to find my next objective.

The visual design of the game is spectacular to the point that, despite the roughness of age, I still find myself marveling at the variety and creativity in the various biomes and explorable locations. I maintain, after having played nearly all of their subsequent releases, that Morrowind is still Bethesda at its most creative and engaging.

"Classic" This game is slow paced and has terrible graphics coupled with some interactions that are questionable at best. Why recommend? because aside from that, this is one of the best games I've ever played. It has everything you would look for in an RPG, and personally, the spell customization is a feature I have not seen rivaled in any other game since. Once you start playing this one, you can't stop.

Morrowind is a beautiful RPG filled with interesting cities to visit, NPC's to engage with and a unique envirenment to explore. Even thogh the game definetly doesn't have the best visuals (something to expect of a game released in 2002), it definetly makes up with it's distinct art design, soundtrack and story. It's a must play for every Elder Scrolls fan and everyone who enjoys RPG's overall!

Very nice RPG =) graphics can not hold with TES IV Oblivion or TES V Skyrim and i have some bugs while leaving but story-like and quests I like very much.
8/10p

This is not a game for the impacient, graphics fanatics or adrenaline junkies.

Morrowind is most definitely one of the most thoughtful games I've ever played. Every piece of clothing has ties to the history of the game world, every place on the game map feels like it was meant to be there, and the majority of content is simply delightful.

The game has a great story, swaths of content, in my opinion fun gameplay and a huge selection of mods. Very few reasons not to get it.

Hey bud, you want a heart-wrenching story of friendship and betrayal where you play the reincarnation of a kind and heroic man murdered by his closest friends who have since ascended to a false godhood and ruled a region with an iron grip ever since? Where you are constantly murdered by shrieking hellbeasts? Where a Daedra threatens to violate you? Where it's a vital part of the game to be infected with a zombie disease? Where everything you try to hit misses? Where your esteemed mentor is absolutely doing crack cocaine and you sleep next to his skooma pipe every night and cry until morning where an assassin attempts to punch your face in at a mere level 2?

Sure ya do.

I think this is the best of the Elder Scrolls, despite the rather dated early 2000's graphics. Where the rest of the Elder Scrolls take place in a sort of generic medieval fantasy world, Morrowind is different and weird in a good way.

The definitive Elder Scrolls experience.

Sure the game might have combat that is outdated to today's standards and use a D20 system. But the story and the world building for the Elder Scrolls III is top notch and I find to be more engaging and better than Elder Scrolls IV and Elder Scrolls V respectively. The mod Tamriel Rebuilt adds so much flavor to the world and just makes it much more immersive than what it already is and I would recommend that mod for any newcomer to Morrowind.

On my first playthrough, at level 12, without even looking at the main quest, I decided to rush the end-game area. I stumbled across the final dungeon, fought my way to the boss, saved the game, attacked him, got killed by him, then reloaded and teleported back to safety, JUST TO SEE IF I COULD. I could.
This game is hands down one of my favourite rpgs out there. I know everyone complains about the dice roll combat, but once you get over that there is so much more Morrowind has to offer.

If i had reviewed this through my first play through i would've not recommend it but until my 2nd the game has shined a lot! I understood the combat system faster then before, the whole "Read to progress the game" system is logical and not to mention... Dagoth Ur is an cool Elder scrolls Antagonist.

This is easily the best RPG I have ever played. It may not look as awesome as Skyrim, but it's values lay in other aspects. It is way more complex than Skyrim can ever dream to be. It has a great sense of adventure, since there is no compass or quest marker to lead you to your quest goal. I'd recommend it for people who think that Skyrim is too easy. Anybody else should stay away, as it is unforgiving. It is not nearly as hard as Dark Souls, but weapon and armour degradation, stamina loss in combat (this results in much weaker hits and reduced accuracy) and enemy types that are immune to conventional attacks, so one has to rely on enchanted weaponry or magic, do not put this game on the easy side of RPGs, even on the easiest setting.

Left seyda neen. First step out tried to stab a slug only missed and died. Restarted used bow and arrow reticle over slug. Miss and die. Restart use magic, all spells fail and slug eats me. Stab a cliff racer, get swarmed by 20 and tossed off the mountain while running. 10/10 would get eaten again.

Oldie but a goldie. Many gameplay elements are heavily outdated by today's standards. However, looking past the age of the game lies something that many RPGs lack today. The game does not hold your hand, as it leaves you figurely many things out by yourself as soon as you leave the brief intro tutorial. If you are purchasing this game, you have to actually put in a lot of commitment to fully enjoy it, and there's A LOT to enjoy.

8.2/10

The elder scrolls game that I have had the most fun with. Yes I have more hours in Skyrim but I enjoyed almost every moment with this game. Don't claim it's nostalgia because this game is older then me and I played it for the first ever a year or so ago and have slowly made my way through it. there's so many positive things to say about the game to the mechanics and levelling system which so many people complain about but once you get the hang of it and know what you're doing it's so much fun and the overall atmosphere is refreshing in a way. the whole game feels like a new experience at every moment and I would definitely recommend it as long as you aren't going to play for 2 hours and then quit because you can't be bothered to figure out what you're meant to do

Graphics - Easily the best graphics ever achieved by mankind. 10/10.
Sound - Absolutely stunning grandmaster tier sound effects and music. 10/10.
Gameplay - A truly unique gameplay experience, the most dynamic combat system out of all Elder Scrolls titles. 10/10.
Story - The story and the lore expands into real life, without a doubt the best fantasy world ever made and with it comes the coolest history and lore of any game I've played. 10/10.

Welcome to the best RPG you'll ever play in your life. Morrowind is a strange land filled with even stranger creatures, and this immersive world combined with a fascinating plot makes for a very grand game indeed. The graphics may not have aged very well, but hey, there's a mod for that (look up Morrowind Overhaul, it's well worth it), and the combat mechanics leave something to be desired, but very few games will sweep your imagination of its feet like this game does. A must-play and a solid 5/5.

Undoubtly one of the best RPG that defines it's genre to the core !
amazing character customization for its time and countless armor customization.

I bought this game way back in 2017, I was a Skybaby back then so I lasted about 40mins "Couldn't hit anything" and refunded it, now I've rebought it, watched a handful of videos, learned how the game works.

And I can say with absolute certainty that this is probably the best Elder Scrolls game, it's actually a real RPG that requires critical thinking, build planning and just big balls. Skyrim introduced me to the series but man that game is so shallow and easy, I can't even call Skyrim a RPG anymore its more like Far Cry with a Fantasy skin.

My first Elder Scrolls game was Skyrim, and I loved it. It still might be my favorite game of all time. After Skyrim, I bought both Oblivion and Morrowind. I got right into Oblivion and it was also great. However, it took me years to get into Morrowind. I spent hours researching builds and then trying them out in Seyda Neen only to quit and try again months later. But finally, I got into it. It's not for everyone. It's not a modern game by any stretch. But for the price, and the feeling you get if you become rabidly interested, I think it is worth it.

I know i have only 18 mins on the record, but I was playing Morrowind before I had bought it on Steam. A classic and a good game for those who are fans of TES universe. Despite its age and graphics, it is still one of the best RPGs ever made.
